decisions.reason: The accelerator is somewhat adjacent to the firm's advisory and partnership capabilities and can strengthen learning from startups, so despite weaker fit than core machinery it is still worth retaining for now.

A bio-based bitumen binder is the weakest fit with the firm's core machinery-and-systems knowledge base, so absorptive-capacity logic suggests limited ability to refine and scale it relative to better-aligned opportunities.

An infectious-waste decontamination plant is close to the firm's established waste-treatment technology base and benefits from partner-linked knowledge, making it a product the firm can likely improve and commercialize.
The mobile mechanical recycling plant sits squarely in the firm's core modular recycling know-how, giving management strong confidence that in-house R&D and field learning can further develop it.
